 A competitive cheerleader, gymnast and athlete, Shae Eichele-Gawry never imagined that attempting an advanced stunt at the age of 18 would lead to a life-altering injury – ending her cheerleading career and leaving her with severe, debilitating, undiagnosed pain in her left leg and ankle.
 Despite many surgeries, treatment and therapy, Shae was still in constant pain, and it took more than two years to receive a diagnosis for complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS), widely considered the world’s most painful chronic condition. CRPS affects more than 200,000 people in the U.S. each year, a result of the body severely overreacting to an injury or surgery, causing worsening pain and greater inflammation than normal.
 This condition left Shae struggling with day-to-day life, at times making even the simple task of getting out of bed unbearable. Since her diagnosis, Shae has found lasting relief with the Abbott Proclaim™ DRG System, which treats CRPS by focusing imperceptible, targeted electrical pulses on a specific cluster of nerves on the spine to block pain signals before they reach the brain.
 To find more information about the DRG system, visit aboutyourpain.com
